notes:
A big one - the curve engine got a rework, plus a stack of bug fixes.

**Multiple wave sections per note** - a note can now have any number of independent, non-overlapping sine/triangle sections instead of just one whole-note wave. Shift-click two bend points to pick a section; pick another (non-overlapping) pair for a second one.

**Bezier tangent handles** - double-click a bend point to give it draggable handles that bow the curve approaching/leaving that point, replacing the old diamond "shaper" tool. Old projects' diamonds still play back the same.

**New tools and shortcuts**
- Cut tool: click a note to slice it into two
- Drag either edge of a note now - the left edge trims/extends from the start
- Alt+Y reverses the selected notes in time (FL-style), including each note's own bend curve
- Grid dropdown next to Snap: 1/1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8, 1/12, 1/16 of a beat
- Ctrl+A selects every note
- Ctrl+Up/Down transposes everything an octave when nothing's selected
- Ctrl+right-click zooms all the way out (capped so it can't leave empty space below the keyboard)

**Remembered settings** - theme, scale, snap, loop length, pitch-bend range, MPE channel count and custom background colours are now remembered globally, and stay in sync even if a host restores project state after the editor's already open (this was causing some DAWs to reset everything to defaults on things like FL's clone/copy instance).

**Bug fixes**
- A note already in progress when playback starts (host playhead not at the very top of the loop) was being silently skipped instead of catching up
- Dragging a multi-note ("chord") selection with snap-to-scale on could leave one note stuck in place while others moved
- Wrong on-note pitch label when a note's bend was shaped to start off its base pitch
- MPE Channels number was unreadable in Dark/Graphite theme
- Thinner note ribbons and a smaller misclick-prone gap between neighbouring notes at different pitches
